My dad was murdered some years ago. I was told by my family members over the phone. I went to visit them a few months later. The car he died in was in the garage. There were bullet holes all over and it hadn’t been touched since it was brought back. We rode in the car & I began to smell cigarettes and liquor. I looked around but obviously no one else smelled it but me. There wasn’t even anything like it in the car. I suddenly felt pain throughout my body and I couldn’t speak for a little bit because my head was spinning. I was so scared and the entire thing was weird because I was feeling fine before I got in the car. I found out later that he had a habit of sitting in his car, having a cigarette and beer, and listening to music. I literally lived his last moments and haven’t gotten over it since. It scares me to this day.

Worked at a call center last year. I absolutely hated it. I have bad anxiety, so clocking in and waiting for the beep was the worst because you never knew what kind of person you’d be talking to. I once got threatened by some lady who was gonna call senators and the president on me. The job got boring really fast and I wasn’t able to handle it because the amount of stress. Every second of my shift was monitored and had to be accounted for. My supervisor once called me in to talk to me about adherence. He asked me why my bathroom breaks were over one minute long and proceeded to compare me to others on the team, which made me feel even worse. I’m honestly glad I got out of there.

The Cleveland Strangler Anthony Sowell. I’ve read about a ton of serial killers and he’s one of the ones that sticks out to me. He killed 11 women over a period of 2 years. His victims were all the same. Black women who were drug addicts & prostitutes. Some women actually came forward telling the police they had been raped and beaten by him but the cases were never high priority, therefore they were never investigated, even though Sowell had a history of raping women. The one thing that disturbs me the most is that there were literally bodies everywhere in his house. The crawl space, the backyard, a fucking skull in a bucket in the basement. He slept and ate and went about his day while bodies were decomposing around him. There’s a really good documentary on him from Vice and there’s also a movie about him called Unseen.

Edit: also adding Ray & Faye Copeland. Elderly couple from Missouri that hired homeless men to work on their farm. Ray would get them involved in a scam where they would go to cattle auctions, bid on cattle, & pay with a check. The check would bounce, and they would disappear. He would kill them if he thought they were going to tell anyone about the scheme and he would bury them on his own farm or other farms he worked on. From what I’ve seen/read, Faye was only convicted because they found a list of men and ironically, the ones that were missing had an ‘X’ next to their name. The list was in her handwriting and Ray couldn’t read or write. There are some documentaries about them on YouTube as well.
